diagnosis: The current best is a degenerate, hyperjammed local optimum: over 1,000 pairs lie within about $10^{-15}$ of the maximum cosine, while contact degrees range from 0 for two rattlers to roughly 27 for overloaded hubs. A point in the 8-dimensional tangent space cannot move without violating one of its contacts once it has substantially more than eight active constraints, so single-point relocation and infinitesimal LP steps can only preserve or restore the existing contact topology. This explains why all leading programs have exactly the seed LP-polish score: small shakes return to the same basin, large shakes relax to worse packings and are rejected, and repeated full LP solves consume the time budget, causing several timeouts. The missing structural property is therefore not greater local tightness but a different, more balanced contact graph—with hub overload removed, rattlers integrated, coverage made more uniform, and a collective rearrangement that changes many contacts simultaneously.
